newsitem.title: ITALY: Zanussi head in Olivetti PCs bid - source.
newsitem.headline: Zanussi head in Olivetti PCs bid - source.

text.p: Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of white goods group Zanussi, is working with U.S. financier Edward Gottesman of the Centenary group in a bid to acquire Italian Olivetti's PC business, a source close to Rossignolo said.
"It is true that Rossignolo is working with Gottesman on the Olivetti operation," the source said, but declined to confirm other details in Milan daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Tuesday.
Il Sole 24 Ore said Rossignolo, who apart from heading Zanussi -- owned by Sweden's Electrolux -- has independent business interests, could tip the scales in favour of Gottesman's Centenary Group.
A spokesman for Olivetti declined to comment on the report. The heavily indebted information technology group has said it is seeking buyers for its PC division.
Olivetti's share price jumped to close 7.35 percent higher at 587.3 lire on the Milan stock exchange, just off a session high of 591 lire in volume of nearly 55 million shares.

Centenary had already signed a declaration of intent and lawyers were already working on a contract of sale for the PC business, Il Sole said, adding that both parties were hoping to finalise the deal by the end of January.

The report said if the deal worked out Rossignolo would probably be the non-executive chairman of an Italian company that would be constituted to take charge of Olivetti's PC interests. It was not yet clear whether Rossignolo intended to acquire a stake in the venture, Il Sole added.
